sub_scenario.one_line: urban planning analyst: reject until the records alcove is available

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the zoning impact assessment and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The permit-counter hot desks review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I wrote the riverfront zoning assessment in the records alcove after mapping every parcel comment to the ordinance.
How did the setting affect it?
The uninterrupted map check kept the recommendation consistent.
Someone new shadowed me in the Wednesday council packet this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the municipal records alcove into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the permit-counter hot desks records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I can explain permit steps to residents from the public counter.
Does that counter work for your day-to-day service?
Yes, for a single question at a time.
I archived last cycle's notes on the permit-counter hot desks and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I confirmed next week's permit-counter hot desks slots with the team.
Any conflicts?
None that survived five minutes.
A vendor call about the zoning impact assessment ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the Wednesday council packet checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the municipal records alcove.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the permit-counter hot desks records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine municipal records alcove cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the municipal records alcove before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the zoning impact assessment updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I moved my reminders so the zoning impact assessment review lands before the weekly sync.
Small automation helps.
It adds up over a quarter.
I compared two options for the permit-counter hot desks tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the Wednesday council packet handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Why should I turn down the permit-counter hot desk before the zoning impact assessment goes into Wednesday's council packet?
